items.title: AI投資熱潮也撐不住？美國8月製造業生產意外創近一年最大降幅
items.title_en: Even the AI Investment Boom Can't Hold? US August Manufacturing Production Unexpectedly Posts Largest Decline in Nearly a Year
paras: 美國8月製造業生產意外下滑，結束連續7個月成長，也是今年以來首次萎縮，顯示在原物料成本攀升及供應鏈受阻之際，製造業回升動能暫時踩下煞車。
聯準會(Fed)周五(18日)公布，美國8月製造業生產較前月下降0.3%，不僅低於7月的成長0.2%，也與《路透》和《彭博》調查經濟學家預期的成長0.3%完全相反，並創2025年10月以來最大單月降幅。與去年同期相比，製造業生產仍成長0.9%。
涵蓋製造業、礦業及公用事業的整體工業生產較前月持平，同樣不及市場預期的成長0.3%。其中，電力需求增加帶動公用事業生產成長1.8%，礦業生產小幅上升，但仍不足以抵銷製造業的疲弱表現。
美國製造業今年以來主要受到企業資本支出、人工智慧(AI)基礎設施建設及消費需求穩健支撐。然而，生產商目前正面臨油價與其他原料成本上漲，以及中東和烏克蘭戰爭引發的供應鏈干擾。
Fed報告顯示，8月商業設備生產下降0.5%，國防與太空設備生產下滑1.2%，扭轉先前數月的強勁表現；不過，兩者生產規模仍明顯高於去年同期。建築用品、家用電子產品及資訊處理設備的生產也同步下降。
從產業類別觀察，電腦與電子產品、家具及基本金屬生產走低，機械、服飾及紡織品則有所增加。汽車生產較前月下滑1.2%；即使排除汽車，製造業生產仍下降0.2%，顯示疲弱情況並非只集中於汽車產業。
衡量工廠潛在產能使用程度的製造業產能利用率降至75.7%，創5個月新低，整體工業產能利用率則維持不變。8月實際生產下滑，也與今年以來明顯回升的ISM製造業調查形成落差，使外界再次質疑企業信心調查能否準確反映實際生產活動。
paras_en: US August manufacturing production unexpectedly fell, ending seven consecutive months of growth and marking the first contraction this year, showing that amid rising raw material costs and supply chain disruptions, the momentum of manufacturing recovery has temporarily hit the brakes.

The Federal Reserve announced on Friday (the 18th) that US manufacturing production in August declined 0.3% from the previous month, not only below July's 0.2% growth but also opposite to economists surveyed by Reuters and Bloomberg who expected a 0.3% increase, and it represents the largest monthly drop since October 2025. Compared with the same period last year, manufacturing production still grew 0.9%.

Overall industrial production, which includes manufacturing, mining and utilities, was flat month‑over‑month, also missing the market’s expected 0.3% growth. Within that, higher electricity demand drove utility production up 1.8%, mining output rose slightly, but it was insufficient to offset the weak manufacturing performance.

This year, US manufacturing has been mainly supported by corporate capital spending, AI infrastructure construction and solid consumer demand. However, producers are now facing higher oil and other raw material costs, as well as supply‑chain disruptions caused by the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine.

The Fed report shows that business equipment production fell 0.5% in August, with defense and space equipment output down 1.2%, reversing the strong performance of previous months; nevertheless, the scale of both remains well above the same month last year. Production of construction supplies, household electronics and information processing equipment also declined.

By industry category, production of computers and electronic products, furniture and basic metals fell, while machinery, apparel and textiles increased. Automobile production slipped 1.2% from the prior month; even excluding autos, manufacturing production still fell 0.2%, indicating that the weakness is not confined to the automotive sector.

The manufacturing capacity utilization rate, which measures the degree of potential factory capacity use, dropped to 75.7%, a five‑month low, while the overall industrial capacity utilization remained unchanged. The August drop in actual production also diverges from the sharply rebounding ISM manufacturing survey this year, prompting renewed doubts about whether business‑confidence surveys can accurately reflect real production activity.

items.title_en: U.S. Companies' Profits Too Good, Suspected Bubble! Goldman Says Don't Fear: S&P 500 Could Reach 8,700 Points
paras: 高盛(GS-US)策略師認為，美國企業強勁獲利背後有經濟展望穩健及人工智慧(AI)投資熱潮支撐，市場擔心企業正形成「盈餘泡沫」的說法言過其實。即使未來獲利增速可能放緩，也不至於出現全面崩跌。
《彭博》彙整數據顯示，標普500指數成分企業今年前兩季獲利均大增約30%，寫下歷來最佳表現之一，全年獲利預期更是2021年新冠疫情後經濟重啟以來最強。
高盛Ben Snider領導的策略團隊指出，AI投資激增可能讓企業目前處於「超額獲利」狀態，但市場定價並未盲目假設高獲利能夠永久延續，而是在預期盈餘繼續成長的同時，仍對當前利潤率能否維持抱持合理懷疑。
美股自8月創下歷史新高後，受到通膨疑慮影響而走弱。即使分析師持續上調盈餘預估，標普500指數估值仍有所下降。市場共識預估，標普500企業2027年及2028年獲利將分別成長19%與17%。
高盛預估相對保守，認為2027年獲利將成長11%。隨著AI投資帶來的提振效果自2027年起逐漸減弱，企業獲利增速可能降溫，即使資本支出仍持續增加，半導體相關公司的利潤率擴張速度也可能放慢。
不過，Snider仍預期標普500指數未來一年將上漲14%，升至約8,700點，主要動力來自企業盈餘成長，而非估值進一步膨脹。他年初便是華爾街較為樂觀的策略師之一，並正確預測強勁獲利及AI普及足以抵銷油價上漲與升息衝擊，使美股多頭行情得以延續。
相較之下，美國銀行(BAC-US)策略師警告，考量企業獲利增速即將放緩，投資人持倉仍過度樂觀。根據美銀引述EPFR Global的數據，美國股票基金單周吸引近640億美元資金流入，創3個月來最大規模。
paras_en: Goldman Sachs (GS-US) strategists argue that the strong earnings of U.S. companies are backed by a solid economic outlook and a wave of artificial‑intelligence (AI) investment, and that market worries about an "earnings bubble" are overstated. Even if earnings growth slows in the future, a broad crash is not inevitable.

Bloomberg’s compiled data show that S&P 500 constituent companies saw earnings jump about 30% in the first two quarters of this year, marking one of the best performances on record, and the full‑year earnings outlook is the strongest since the economy rebooted after the 2021 COVID‑19 pandemic.

Goldman’s strategy team led by Ben Snider notes that the surge in AI spending may put companies in a "excess earnings" situation, but market pricing does not blindly assume that high earnings will last forever; while earnings are expected to keep growing, investors remain reasonably skeptical about whether current profit margins can be sustained.

U.S. equities weakened after hitting historic highs in August due to inflation concerns. Even as analysts keep raising earnings forecasts, the S&P 500 valuation has slipped. The market consensus projects that S&P 500 companies’ earnings will grow 19% in 2027 and 17% in 2028.

Goldman’s estimates are relatively conservative, forecasting an 11% earnings growth for 2027. As the boost from AI investment wanes from 2027 onward, earnings growth may cool, and even though capital spending will keep rising, the rate of margin expansion for semiconductor‑related firms could slow.

Nevertheless, Snider still expects the S&P 500 to rise 14% over the next year, reaching roughly 8,700 points, driven mainly by corporate earnings growth rather than further valuation expansion. He was one of Wall Street’s more optimistic strategists at the start of the year and correctly predicted that strong earnings and widespread AI adoption would offset higher oil prices and rate‑hike impacts, allowing the bull market to continue.

In contrast, strategists at Bank of America (BAC-US) warn that, given the impending slowdown in corporate earnings growth, investors remain overly optimistic in their positions. Citing EPFR Global data, BofA notes that U.S. equity funds attracted about $64 billion of net inflows in a single week, the largest in three months.

items.title: 7兆美元選擇權同時到期！美股迎歷來第二大「三巫日」
items.title_en: $7 trillion of Options Expire Simultaneously! US Stocks Face the Second‑Largest Ever “Triple Witch Day”
paras: 美股周五(18日)迎來規模罕見的「三巫日」，約有7兆美元名目價值的美國選擇權集中到期，相當於整體市場約四分之一，可能加劇盤勢波動。
根據Citadel Securities統計，本次包括標普500指數月選擇權、個股選擇權等衍生性商品同時到期，規模將是歷來第二大，其中約60%會在開盤時完成結算或展期。
Citadel Securities由Scott Rubner領導的市場情報團隊指出，這次到期潮可能重新改寫市場的技術面環境。過去一段時間，選擇權部位配置在一定程度上壓低了實際波動，但當相關部位到期或向後展期後，原先抑制波動的力量可能明顯減弱。
這意味著，市場在選擇權到期後可能更容易受到股票買賣資金流向影響，價格波動也可能因此放大。尤其美國10年期公債殖利率再度逼近5%，市場同時評估聯準會(Fed)後續升息前景，龐大選擇權部位集中退場，可能讓原本已缺乏明確方向的美股更加敏感。
不過，三巫日本身不必然導致股市下跌，主要影響在於交易量與盤中震盪可能增加。投資人將觀察部位結算後，交易商是否需要重新進行避險，以及失去原有選擇權部位支撐後，市場能否維持穩定。
paras_en: US equities on Friday (the 18th) saw a rare “Triple Witch Day” as about $7 trillion of American options expired at once, roughly a quarter of the whole market, which could amplify market volatility.

According to Citadel Securities’ data, this batch includes S&P 500 index monthly options, single‑stock options and other derivatives, making it the second‑largest expiration ever, with about 60% expected to be settled or rolled over at the opening.

Citadel’s market‑intelligence team, led by Scott Rubner, said the expiration wave could rewrite the market’s technical landscape. Recently, the options positioning has been dampening actual volatility, but once those positions expire or are rolled forward, the suppressive force on volatility may weaken markedly.

That means after the options expire, the market may become more susceptible to stock‑buying and selling flows, potentially magnifying price swings. With the US 10‑year Treasury yield again edging toward 5%, the market is also weighing the Fed’s future rate‑hike outlook, and the massive unwind of options could make an already directionless equity market even more sensitive.

However, the Triple Witch Day itself does not necessarily cause a market decline; the main impact is likely higher trading volume and intraday turbulence. Investors will watch whether dealers need to re‑hedge after the positions settle and whether the market can stay stable after losing the support of the original options positions.

items.title: 日銀總裁的「鷹派立場」未讓市場理解及接受 日元跌勢加劇
items.title_en: Bank of Japan Governor's Hawkish Stance Not Understood or Accepted by Market, Yen Decline Accelerates
paras: 日本央行總裁植田和男周五(18日)在記者會上，傳達出對於升息更為積極的鷹派姿態，然而日元不僅未能止跌，跌勢反倒進一步擴大。分析師指出，主因是植田的說法未讓投資者理解及滿意。
日本外匯市場周五傍晚，日元兌美元匯率一度跌至157區間後段，較紐約市場收盤時的跌幅達1.2%。日本央行在貨幣政策會議上將政策利率從之前的1%上調至1.25%，植田則重申繼續升息立場。

短期承壓：政策訊息混淆

Reed Capital 投資總監 Gerald Gan 表示，儘管植田試圖平息市場情緒，但他仍維持短期內日元將持續疲軟的看法，並強調日銀與美國聯準會(Fed)在前瞻指引上的分歧，正成為影響日元穩定的主要疑慮。
富國銀行(Wells Fargo)亞太區策略負責人 Chidu Narayana 指出，植田的鷹派態度不足以支持市場原本過於激進的期待，在缺乏明確鷹派信號與美元反彈下，美元兌日元匯率將維持高位。
Stonex Financial 利率主管 Shriya Samarth 認為，日銀傳遞的訊息相當混淆，既承認政策優先順序改變，又不願承諾面對通膨上行風險，難以被市場認定為足夠鷹派。T&D 資產管理首席策略師Hiroshi Namioka補充，市場難解讀植田的發言，導致日元短暫走強後再度重回貶勢。

結構性壓力與市場干預風險

Pictet Asset Management Japan 投資策略部長田中純平分析，植田宣示「政策營運階段改變」，雖有助於消除市場對日銀落後於曲線的疑慮，但受制於日元面臨的結構性下行壓力，加上市場預期的日美升息步調差異有限，僅憑本次會議結果難以觸發持續性的日元升值行情。
此外，他提醒連休期間交易清淡，投資人仍需戒備日美政府進行協調干預的可能性，預期美元兌日元將持續劇烈波動且缺乏明確方向。

部分分析師看好日元中長期走升

不過，部分分析師持較為樂觀的態度。SMBC 信託銀行投資調查部長山口真弘認為，植田成功化解了記者會可能引發日元急跌的風險，且日銀的基本立場並未改變，市場仍維持每3個月升息一次(如今年 12 月)的預期，因此不認為日元會陷入長期走貶趨勢。
State Street Investment Management 資深固定收益策略師Masahiko Loo強調，市場不應過度解讀兩位審議委員的反對票，美元兌日元在 160 附近仍宜採取逢高賣出策略。他預測，隨著日銀政策正常化帶動國內殖利率上升、日本資產吸引機構資金回流，以及 AI 相關投資增加等三大結構性因素，日元中長期走勢將逐漸獲得支撐。
paras_en: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda on Friday (the 18th) conveyed a more aggressive hawkish stance toward rate hikes at a press conference, yet the yen not only failed to stop falling, its decline actually widened. Analysts said the main reason was that Ueda's remarks did not resonate with or satisfy investors.

In the Japanese foreign‑exchange market on Friday evening, the yen slipped to the lower end of the 157 range against the dollar, a 1.2% drop from the New York close. The BOJ raised its policy rate from 1.0% to 1.25% at its monetary‑policy meeting, and Ueda reiterated the commitment to continue raising rates.

Short‑term pressure: mixed policy signals
Gerald Gan, Investment Director at Reed Capital, said that despite Ueda’s attempt to calm market sentiment, he still expects the yen to remain weak in the short run and highlighted the growing divergence between the BOJ and the U.S. Federal Reserve on forward guidance as a key concern for yen stability.

Chidu Narayana, Head of Asia‑Pacific Strategy at Wells Fargo, noted that Ueda’s hawkish tone was insufficient to meet the market’s overly aggressive expectations, and without a clear hawkish signal and a dollar rebound, the dollar‑yen pair is likely to stay elevated.

Shriya Samarth, Head of Rates at Stonex Financial, said the BOJ’s messaging was quite confusing – it acknowledged a shift in policy priorities but was unwilling to commit to tackling upside inflation risks, making it hard for the market to view the stance as sufficiently hawkish. Hiroshi Namioka, Chief Strategist at T&D Asset Management, added that the market struggled to interpret Ueda’s comments, causing a brief yen rally that quickly reverted to depreciation.

Structural pressure and intervention risk
Junpei Tanaka, Head of Investment Strategy for Japan at Pictet Asset Management, analyzed that Ueda’s declaration of a “change in the policy operating phase” helps allay concerns that the BOJ is lagging behind the yield curve, but the yen faces structural downward pressure and the expected gap between Japan and U.S. rate‑hiking paths is limited, so the meeting outcome alone is unlikely to trigger a sustained yen appreciation rally.

He also warned that trading is thin over the holiday period and investors should remain vigilant about the possibility of coordinated intervention by Japanese and U.S. authorities, expecting the dollar‑yen to continue swinging wildly with no clear direction.

Some analysts are bullish on the yen over the medium to long term
Nevertheless, a few analysts are more optimistic. Masahiro Yamaguchi, Head of Investment Research at SMBC Trust Bank, believes Ueda successfully defused the risk of a sharp yen drop that could have arisen from the press conference, and that the BOJ’s fundamental stance remains unchanged. The market still expects a rate hike every three months (e.g., in December), so he does not see the yen entering a long‑term downtrend.

Masahiko Loo, Senior Fixed‑Income Strategist at State Street Investment Management, stressed that the market should not over‑interpret the dissenting votes of two board members. He recommends selling on rallies near the 160 level for the dollar‑yen. He forecasts that as BOJ policy normalises, domestic yields rise, Japanese assets attract institutional inflows, and AI‑related investments grow, three structural factors will gradually support the yen’s medium‑ to long‑term trajectory.

items.title: 升息為何讓日元重摔、日股大漲？解析日銀決策被解讀不夠鷹派的三大關鍵
paras: 日本銀行(央行，BOJ)周五(18日)將升息1碼(25個基點)至1.25%，利率創1995年以來最高，且升息間隔從之前的六個月縮短為三個月。儘管升息步調加快，日本金融市場卻出現違反直覺的走勢：日元走弱、10年期日本公債殖利率下滑，日經225指數上漲。
分析師指出，日銀理事會表決出現兩張反對升息票，加上本次升息並未同步公布最新經濟展望，都讓市場解讀日銀不夠鷹派。
目前市場預期，日銀可能在12月左右再次升息，但對利率最終將升至多高卻看法不一。
升息通常會帶動一國貨幣上揚、推升債券殖利率，並對股市造成壓力，但日本的貨幣、債券殖利率與股市周五卻出現完全相反的走勢。截稿前，日元跌破157日元兌1美元，10年期日本政府公債殖利率下滑，日經225指數收盤上漲1.4%。

升息決策7票對2票 市場解讀不夠鷹派

專家指出，日銀理事會出現分歧，是市場出現非典型反應的原因，因為這顯示日本央行可能不會採取過於鷹派的立場。
日本銀行三井住友銀行(SMBC)首席外匯策略師Hirofumi Suzuki說：「兩票反對升息、主張維持利率不變，令人感到意外。」
本次升息決策以七票對兩票通過，理事淺田統一郎(Toichiro Asada)與佐藤綾野(Ayano Sato)投下反對票，他們是由首相高市早苗今年稍早任命、被視為恢復通膨派的人馬。
佐藤綾野指出，由於核心通膨率低於2%，經濟情勢可能還不夠強勁，因此主張維持利率不變。日本8月核心通膨率微降至1.7%，低於7月的1.8%。
淺田統一郎也表示，與先前相比，目前經濟與物價發展似乎沒有大幅加速。

未同步更新經濟展望

道富投資管理公司(State Street Investment Management)資深固定收益策略師Masahiko Loo指出，此次升息未同步公布更新版的經濟展望報告，也是市場反直覺回應的原因之一，因為這限制了日銀透過調整預測來強化鷹派訊息的能力。
牛津經濟學(Oxford Economics)日本經濟主管Shigeto Nagai認同這項看法，他表示，兩名反對升息的理事傳遞的訊號是，高市早苗並未確定接受美國要求日本加快升息的主張。
路透周五報導，美國財長貝森特(Scott Bessent)5月與日本財務大臣片山皋月(Satsuki Katayama)會面時，曾強調日銀需要提高利率。
Nagai進一步補充說：「其次，如果我們觀察聲明，所有措辭與語氣幾乎都與7月公布的季度展望報告相同，因此語氣不像金融市場原本期待的那麼鷹派。」

利率還能升多少？

專家目前認為，日銀可能在12月左右再次升息。
道富的Loo表示，他預期日銀總裁植田和男將強調，未來每一次政策會議都仍然「有可能升息」。他說：「如今爭論的已經不是日銀是否升息，而是利率最終會升到多高。」
日銀表示，隨著經濟與物價情勢發展，將持續調升利率。不過，日銀也承認，中東衝突推升油價，可能導致經濟成長放緩。
EFG International經濟學家Sam Jochim表示，隨著潛在通膨率接近2%，利率可能大約每三個月調升一次。他預期，2027年的終點利率、也就是利率可能達到的峰值，將落在1.75%至2%之間。
BOJ並未預測終點利率，而是持續表示將「適當」執行貨幣政策，以讓潛在通膨率穩定在約2%的目標。
穆迪分析(Moody’s Analytics)亞太區經濟主管Stefan Angrick預期，日銀可能在今年底至明年初再度升息，但需求帶動的通膨疲弱，加上實質薪資成長令人失望，將限縮後續的升息幅度。

items.title: 不排除更大幅度或連續升息！日本央行總裁：貨幣政策進入「新階段」
items.title_en: BOJ Governor Says Monetary Policy Has Entered a "New Phase"; Larger or Consecutive Rate Hikes Not Ruled Out
paras: 日本央行(BOJ)今(18)日結束兩天會議，決定把無擔保隔夜拆款利率目標由1%上調1碼至1.25%，為1995年以來最高水準，該決議以7票贊成、2票反對通過，距6月升息僅時隔三個月，是1990年來間隔最短的連續升息。
BOJ總裁植田和男在會後記者會上表示，基礎通膨率逐步接近2%，日本貨幣政策「已進入新階段」，未來升息節奏與幅度將按物價形勢逐次判斷，不設定「每三個月加一次」等固定路徑。若基礎通膨有持續超過2%的風險，不排除更大幅度或連續升息，但終端利率與中性利率目前難精確界定，將在實際緊縮中慢慢校準。
根據BOJ聲明，物價存在向上偏離2%目標的風險，將繼續依經濟、物價與金融情勢調整寬鬆程度，制定政策時重點看中東局勢、AI需求與匯率傳導。
植田和男指出，中東危機已帶動第二輪物價上漲，油價、進口成本與企業轉價壓力均需警惕，避免通膨明顯超標後被迫劇烈緊縮。
8月數據呈「表面放緩、底層仍緊」。根據日本總務省公布的CPI數據，8月年增率1.9%，剔除鮮食核心CPI年增1.7%、低於7月1.8%，剔除鮮食與能源的核心指標漲1.9%，而政府能源等補貼壓低8月CPI約0.62個百分點。同期，企業物價指數年增7.6%，有色金屬、資通設備、石油煤炭分別大漲，日元計價進口物價年增24.8%，顯示上游成本正往終端傳導。
2張反對票也反映BOJ內部分歧。淺田統一郎認為，核心通膨率仍低於2%，經濟尚不足以支持再度升息；佐藤綾野主張觀察6月升息效果，不急於9月行動。兩人反對及植田「未給下次明確時間表」的事實，削弱市場對BOJ快速連續升息的預期。
金融市場呈「買預期、賣事實」。BOJ決議出爐後，日元兌美元一度貶破157，日本10年期國債殖利率回落，日經225收漲約1.4%。通常，升息會支撐本國貨幣與長債利率，但本次因反對票、缺乏更鷹前瞻，加上美債與Fed升息預期壓住美日利差，日元與日債未獲明顯提振。
分析人士指出，後續焦點轉向今年內BOJ是否再次升息、企業夏季獎金與2027年春鬥薪情能否讓基礎通膨穩住2%；若油價、日元貶值與批發物價繼續向上，BOJ即便內部分歧，仍可能維持每季度評估、漸進推高政策利率。
paras_en: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) concluded its two‑day meeting today (the 18th), raising the uncollateralised overnight call rate target from 1.0% to 1.25% – a 0.25‑percentage‑point increase and the highest level since 1995. The decision passed 7‑to‑2, marking the shortest interval between consecutive hikes since 1990, just three months after the June increase.

BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda told reporters after the meeting that the underlying inflation rate is gradually approaching 2% and that Japan’s monetary policy "has entered a new phase." Future rate‑hike timing and magnitude will be judged case‑by‑case based on price developments, with no preset path such as "every three months." If the core inflation risk of staying above 2% persists, larger or back‑to‑back hikes are not ruled out, although the terminal and neutral rates are currently hard to pin down and will be calibrated gradually as tightening proceeds.

According to the BOJ statement, price pressures pose a risk of deviating upward from the 2% target, and the bank will continue to adjust the degree of easing in line with economic, price and financial conditions, paying particular attention to the Middle‑East situation, AI demand and exchange‑rate transmission when formulating policy.

Ueda noted that the Middle‑East crisis has sparked a second round of price increases, with oil prices, import costs and corporate pass‑through pressures all requiring vigilance to avoid a scenario where inflation clearly overshoots the target and forces a sharp tightening.

August data showed a "surface slowdown but underlying tightness." Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications CPI data showed an annual increase of 1.9% in August, with core CPI (excluding fresh food) up 1.7% year‑on‑year, down from 1.8% in July. Core CPI excluding fresh food and energy rose 1.9%, while government energy subsidies trimmed the August CPI by about 0.62 percentage points. In the same period, the corporate goods price index rose 7.6% year‑on‑year, with large jumps in non‑ferrous metals, ICT equipment and oil‑coal; import prices priced in yen surged 24.8% year‑on‑year, indicating upstream cost pressures are passing through to the end‑user.

The two dissenting votes also reflected internal divisions at the BOJ. Ichiro Asada argued that core inflation remains below 2% and the economy is not strong enough to support another hike; Ayano Sato advocated waiting to see the effect of the June hike and said there was no rush to act in September. Their opposition, together with Ueda’s lack of a clear timetable for the next move, weakened market expectations of rapid consecutive hikes.

Financial markets displayed a "buy the expectation, sell the fact" pattern. After the BOJ decision, the yen briefly fell past ¥157 per dollar, 10‑year Japanese government bond yields retreated, and the Nikkei 225 rose about 1.4%. Typically, a rate hike supports the domestic currency and long‑term bond yields, but this time the dissenting votes, the absence of a more hawkish outlook, and U.S. Treasury and Fed rate‑hike expectations compressing the yen‑U.S. yield spread kept the yen and JGBs from receiving a clear boost.

Analysts said the next focus will be whether the BOJ will hike again within the year, corporate summer bonuses and whether 2027 spring‑time wage negotiations can keep core inflation anchored at 2%. If oil prices, yen depreciation and wholesale prices keep rising, the BOJ may still move forward with quarterly assessments and incremental policy‑rate increases despite internal disagreements.

items.title: 「川習會」前夕人民幣強勢突破6.70關卡 創逾4年新高
items.title_en: Ahead of the ‘Xi‑Trump Meeting’, the RMB Breaks Through the 6.70 Barrier, Reaching a Four‑Year High
paras: 在美中元首即將會面及美國聯準會宣布升息的背景下，在岸與離岸人民幣對美元匯率周五(18日)雙雙升破 6.70 關卡，創下逾4年來新高。
離岸人民幣對美元周五亞市盤中最高升至 6.6935 至 6.6953，在岸人民幣即期匯率升破 6.70 關卡，觸及 6.6954 至 6.6975。中國人民銀行將人民幣對美元中間價設為 6.7521，連續第八個交易日上調，創近兩年最長連升紀錄，釋放明確的穩匯率訊號。今年以來，在岸與離岸人民幣對美元累計升值均已超過 4%。
在國際市場方面，美國聯準會剛決議升息一碼至 4%，點陣圖顯示年內可能再升息，帶動美元指數一度衝高。然而，儘管中國 8 月新增貸款遠低於預期、信用需求偏弱，人民幣依然展現抗跌韌性。
市場分析指出，6.70 為重要技術與心理關卡。人行引導匯率偏強，有助於穩定資金預期並緩解資本外流壓力。
此外，中國國家主席習近平預計於 9 月 24 日與美國總統川普會面，分析認為北京在峰會前容許人民幣升值，能降低美方對弱勢匯率的指控，釋放談判善意。
針對本輪升值行情，東方金誠首席宏觀分析師王青指出，走強主因包含聯準會升息效應釋放後美元指數回落，以及中間價偏強調整。王青表示，中國出口持續高增長與經濟穩中有進為匯率築牢基本面。在「宏觀審慎+微觀監管」框架下，不必過度高估升息衝擊，短期內人民幣預計將維持穩中偏強格局。
另一方面，華福證券首席經濟學家管濤則提醒市場應理性看待升值。管濤表示，雖然短期利多因素占優，但升值的宏觀緊縮效應可能干擾市場情緒。長期來看，「雙向波動」將是常態，不宜將升值過度解讀為資產重估，不宜對匯率做過多的價值判斷。
paras_en: Against the backdrop of an upcoming meeting between the U.S. and Chinese heads of state and the Federal Reserve’s rate‑hike announcement, both on‑shore and off‑shore RMB‑USD rates on Friday the 18th surged past the 6.70 mark, setting a new high not seen in over four years.

The offshore RMB rose to a peak of 6.6935‑6.6953 against the dollar during Friday’s Asian session, while the on‑shore spot rate broke the 6.70 barrier, reaching 6.6954‑6.6975. The People’s Bank of China set the RMB‑USD central parity at 6.7521, marking the eighth consecutive trading day of an upward adjustment and the longest streak in nearly two years, sending a clear signal of rate stability. Since the start of the year, both on‑shore and offshore RMB have appreciated by more than 4% against the dollar.

In international markets, the Fed just voted to raise rates by one basis point to 4%, and the dot‑plot suggests another hike could come later this year, briefly pushing the U.S. dollar index higher. Nevertheless, despite August’s new‑loan growth falling well short of expectations and credit demand remaining weak, the RMB has shown resilience against declines.
Analysts note that 6.70 is a key technical and psychological level. The PBOC’s guidance toward a stronger exchange rate helps stabilize funding expectations and eases pressure from capital outflows.

Moreover, Chinese President Xi Jinping is slated to meet U.S. President Donald Trump on September 24. Analysts believe that allowing the RMB to appreciate before the summit can reduce U.S. accusations of a weak currency and signal goodwill in the negotiations.

Commenting on the recent appreciation, Wang Qing, chief macro analyst at Dongfang Jincheng, said the main drivers are the Fed‑rate‑hike effect that has pulled the dollar index back and the relatively strong central parity adjustment. Wang added that China’s continued strong export growth and a stable‑yet‑improving economy provide a solid fundamentals foundation for the currency. Under a “macro‑prudent plus micro‑regulation” framework, the rate‑hike impact should not be over‑estimated, and the RMB is expected to remain stable‑to‑strong in the short term.

On the other hand, Guan Tao, chief economist at Huafu Securities, cautioned that the market should view the appreciation rationally. Guan said that although short‑term bullish factors dominate, the macro‑tightening effect of an appreciating currency could affect market sentiment. In the long run, “two‑way volatility” will be the norm, and the appreciation should not be over‑interpreted as an asset revaluation nor should the exchange rate be subject to excessive value judgments.

U.S. August retail sales were strong and import prices surged, and the Federal Reserve (Fed) raised rates by 25 basis points as expected. Market focus shifted to Friday’s Bank of Japan (BOJ) decision, with most expecting a rate hike to a 31‑year high of 1.25% and a signal that borrowing costs will stay elevated. On Thursday, Japanese Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said Japan will keep close communication with the United States to maintain stable yen movements. Prime Minister Kishida also reshuffled the cabinet, retaining many key ministers to solidify political support amid market turbulence and to push forward her flagship spending plan. Finance Minister Shunichi Suzuki stayed on to ensure continuity in Japan’s exchange‑rate policy, pledging a firm response to excessive yen volatility. items.title: 日本10年債殖利率飆破3% 貝森特「逼宮」日本大撒錢 要求升息、收斂財政支出
items.title_en: Japan 10-Year Bond Yield Surges Past 3% as Bessent Pressures Tokyo to Spend Big, Demand Rate Hikes and Fiscal Tightening
paras: 美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)近幾個月持續向日本政府施壓，要求東京控制大規模財政支出、讓日本央行加快升息，以遏制日元疲弱與通膨壓力。路透引述3名知情人士指出，當日本財務大臣片山皐月(Satsuki Katayama)今年6月22日致電貝森特，希望美國協助支撐大幅走貶的日元時，貝森特反而要求日本先處理財政政策問題，並避免貨幣與財政政策相互矛盾。
這通此前未被公開報導的電話，成為美日兩國7月底大規模聯手干預匯市的前奏。日本方面原本擔心日元疲弱推高通膨，進而傷害首相高市早苗的政治支持度；但貝森特更關注日本公債遭大幅拋售可能波及美國公債市場。日本是美國國債最大的海外持有國，因此日本長期公債殖利率若大幅攀升，可能推高美國政府的借貸成本。
貝森特過去數月已私下向片山及其他日本官員表示，日本應收斂大規模財政支出，同時日本央行需要升息。他在6月通話中再次要求東京處理推低日元的根本因素，並認為高市政府擴大支出的政策，正在削弱日本央行抑制通膨的努力。
貝森特5月在日本與片山會面時，也曾強調日本央行需要提高利率。3名消息人士表示，當時日本政府內部已普遍認為6月或7月升息幾乎勢在必行。日本央行6月升息後，片山一度認為貝森特可能同意美國加入聯合買進日元的行動，但貝森特仍把焦點放在日本財政政策。
7月底，美日最終展開聯合干預匯市。日本首席外匯事務官三村淳(Atsushi Mimura)當時形容，這是日本與美國貨幣合作關係的成果。日本財務省與美國財政部的合作，使日元一度明顯反彈，但這波升值並未持續太久。
數周後，日元重新走弱，美國方面對高市政府未能明顯撤回刺激經濟措施感到失望，加上全球公債殖利率同步攀升，使日本財政問題受到更大關注。8月31日至9月1日舉行的G20財長會議上，貝森特再次要求日本升息並收緊財政政策，且語氣較先前更為強硬。
貝森特此前接受媒體訪問時表示，日本應該「坐下來享受安倍經濟學的成功」，理由是日本長期通縮時代已經過去，目前政策重點應從刺激經濟轉向控制通膨。這被視為美國迄今對高市政府延續安倍經濟學政策最明確的警告之一。
隨著市場持續拋售日本公債，日本10年期基準公債殖利率9月初升破3%關卡，觸及30年高點。日本前最高外匯事務官古澤滿宏(Mitsuhiro Furusawa)指出，日本公共債務規模龐大，需要提出可信的中長期財政展望，並確保貨幣政策與財政政策一致，避免長期利率出現不受歡迎的急升。
在G20會議期間，片山向與會財長保證，日本將降低對額外支出的依賴，也不會透過發行債券來支應減稅。她會後透露，自己曾向貝森特展示高市早苗接受日本媒體《讀賣新聞》訪問時提出的「同時實現經濟成長與財政紀律」主張，貝森特則回應表示認同。
貝森特隨後再度對日元空頭發出警告，並表示自己掌握部分日本政策制定者包括日本央行的非對稱資訊，對政策走向具有較深入的了解。他甚至表示「現在我是莊家」，並稱投資人如果願意可以押注與他相反的方向，相關言論也一度帶動日元升值。
這場美日財政與貨幣政策角力，正值日本央行準備進一步升息之際。日本央行的政策方向大致與貝森特要求提高利率的立場一致，但在財政政策方面，日本政府與美國之間仍存在明顯落差。
高市早苗很難完全撤回帶動其所屬政黨在今年選舉中取得支持的主要刺激政策。政府透過補貼及其他措施降低燃料成本，也有助於緩解民眾對生活成本上升的不滿，因此大幅削減支出可能帶來政治壓力。
另一方面，美國若要求日本大幅縮減減稅與支出計畫，也可能削弱一個重要亞洲盟友的政府穩定性。在美國與中國競爭升溫之際，華府仍重視與日本的安全及經濟合作。美國總統川普在美日共同支撐日元後，也再次強調兩國夥伴關係的重要性。
日本政府周四進行內閣改組，高市早苗重新任命片山皐月擔任財務大臣，被部分市場人士視為兼顧市場信心與政策延續性的安排。片山本身較偏向財政保守立場，近來一方面需要向市場保證日本不會無限制擴大支出，另一方面也必須推動高市政府的投資與經濟政策。
不過，目前並沒有跡象顯示高市政府準備全面放棄擴張性財政政策。日本下一財政年度的預算要求總額已膨脹至143兆日元(約9,161.4億美元)，接近疫情期間的高峰。高市政府則承諾，在截至2028年3月的財政年度，新發行公債規模將維持約40兆日元，高於本年度預估的32.7兆日元。
部分日本官員認為，若考量臨時調降消費稅、增加國防支出以及融資成本上升，要將新發債規模控制在40兆日元左右可能相當困難。日本政府近期公布的食品消費稅減免計畫本身就可能造成約5兆日元的稅收缺口，進一步增加市場對財政健全性的疑慮。
目前這場財政政策僵局尚未演變成更大規模的美日衝突，顯示高市政府與川普政府之間仍保有一定外交空間。不過，部分分析人士認為，貝森特對日本財政政策的施壓，反映川普政府正在把其對盟友的談判方式延伸至金融與財政政策領域。
日本前外匯官員中尾武彥(Takehiko Nakao)表示，美國過去對日本的訊息較偏向要求東京採取正確政策，如今則顯得更直接。美國關切的不只是日元匯率，也包括日本公債市場穩定、通膨政策可信度，以及日本大量持有美國國債對美國融資成本可能造成的影響。
因此，貝森特與日本政府之間的角力已不再只是單純的匯率問題，而是同時牽涉日本央行升息速度、政府支出、減稅、國防預算、日本公債殖利率，以及全球最大兩個政府債券市場之間的相互影響。對高市政府而言，如何在維持經濟刺激政策、控制生活成本與回應金融市場對財政紀律的要求之間取得平衡，將成為後續政策的核心課題。
paras_en: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been pressing the Japanese government for months, urging Tokyo to curb massive fiscal spending and accelerate rate hikes by the Bank of Japan to curb a weak yen and inflation pressures. Reuters, citing three informed sources, said that when Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama called Bessent on June 22 to ask for U.S. support for the sharply depreciating yen, Bessent instead told Japan to first address its fiscal policy issues and avoid contradictions between monetary and fiscal policy.

The previously undisclosed call set the stage for the large‑scale joint FX intervention by the United States and Japan at the end of July. Japan had feared that a weak yen would lift inflation and erode Prime Minister Kishida Nae‑suke’s political support, but Bessent was more worried that a heavy sell‑off of Japanese government bonds could spill over into the U.S. Treasury market. Japan is the largest foreign holder of U.S. Treasuries, so a sharp rise in Japanese long‑term bond yields could push up borrowing costs for the U.S. government.

Bessent has privately told Katayama and other Japanese officials over the past few months that Japan should rein in its massive fiscal outlays while the BOJ needs to raise rates. In the June call he again urged Tokyo to tackle the root causes of yen weakness and argued that the Kishida administration’s expansionary spending was undermining the BOJ’s fight against inflation.

When Bessent met Katayama in Japan in May, he also stressed that the BOJ needed to hike rates. Three sources said that at the time the Japanese government already believed a rate hike in June or July was almost inevitable. After the BOJ raised rates in June, Katayama briefly thought Bessent might agree to a joint yen‑buying operation, but Bessent kept the focus on Japan’s fiscal stance.

At the end of July the U.S. and Japan carried out a joint FX intervention. Japan’s chief foreign exchange official Atsushi Mimura described it as the fruit of monetary cooperation between the two countries. The coordination between Japan’s finance ministry and the U.S. Treasury sparked a noticeable yen rally, but the appreciation was short‑lived.

Weeks later the yen weakened again. The United States expressed disappointment that the Kishida government had not rolled back its stimulus measures, and rising global bond yields heightened scrutiny of Japan’s fiscal situation. At the G20 finance ministers’ meeting on Aug. 31‑Sept. 1, Bessent again demanded that Japan raise rates and tighten fiscal policy, using a tougher tone than before.

In a prior media interview Bessent said Japan should “sit down and enjoy the success of Abenomics,” arguing that the era of chronic deflation is over and policy should shift from stimulus to inflation control. The comment was seen as one of the clearest U.S. warnings to the Kishida administration about continuing Abenomics‑style policies.

As markets kept selling Japanese bonds, the yield on the benchmark 10‑year Japanese government bond broke the 3% barrier in early September, hitting a 30‑year high. Former top FX official Mitsuhiro Furusawa warned that Japan’s huge public debt requires a credible medium‑ to long‑term fiscal outlook and alignment of monetary and fiscal policy to avoid an unwelcome surge in long‑term rates.

During the G20 meeting Katayama assured fellow finance chiefs that Japan would reduce reliance on extra spending and would not fund tax cuts by issuing new bonds. After the meeting she disclosed that she had shown Bessent Kishida’s “grow the economy while maintaining fiscal discipline” pitch given to Yomiuri Shimbun, which Bessent said he agreed with.

Bessent later warned yen short‑sellers again, claiming he possessed asymmetric information about Japanese policymakers, including the BOJ, giving him deeper insight into policy direction. He even said, “Now I am the house,” and suggested investors could bet against him, a remark that briefly boosted the yen.

The U.S.–Japan clash over fiscal and monetary policy comes as the BOJ prepares to raise rates further. The BOJ’s policy trajectory broadly aligns with Bessent’s call for higher rates, but a gap remains on the fiscal side between Japan’s government and Washington.

Kishida finds it hard to fully roll back the stimulus measures that have helped his party gain electoral support this year. Subsidies and other actions that lower fuel costs ease public anger over rising living expenses, so a sharp cut in spending could create political pressure.

Conversely, if the United States demands a major cut in Japan’s tax cuts and spending plans, it could undermine the stability of an important Asian ally. With U.S.–China competition heating up, Washington still values Japan’s security and economic partnership. After the joint effort to support the yen, President Trump again stressed the importance of the bilateral partnership.

Japan reshuffled its cabinet on Thursday, re‑appointing Katayama as finance minister under Kishida, a move some market participants saw as balancing market confidence with policy continuity. Katayama leans fiscally conservative and now must reassure markets that Japan will not expand spending unchecked while still advancing Kishida’s investment and economic agenda.

Nevertheless, there is no sign that the Kishida administration is ready to abandon its expansionary fiscal stance. The budget request for the next fiscal year has swelled to ¥143 trillion (about $9.16 billion), near the pandemic‑era peak. The government has pledged that new bond issuance for the fiscal year ending March 2028 will stay around ¥40 trillion, above the current‑year estimate of ¥32.7 trillion.

Some officials argue that, given a temporary cut to the consumption tax, higher defence spending and rising financing costs, keeping new issuance near ¥40 trillion will be very difficult. The recently announced food‑tax relief plan could create a ¥5 trillion revenue gap, further raising doubts about fiscal soundness.

The fiscal standoff has not yet escalated into a broader U.S.–Japan clash, indicating that diplomatic space remains between the Kishida and Trump administrations. However, some analysts say Bessent’s pressure on Japan’s fiscal policy reflects the Trump administration’s habit of extending its negotiating style with allies into financial and fiscal realms.

Former FX official Takehiko Nakao said the United States used to mainly tell Tokyo to adopt the right policies, but now its messaging is more direct. Washington’s concerns cover not only the yen rate but also the stability of Japan’s bond market, the credibility of its inflation policy and the impact of Japan’s large U.S. Treasury holdings on U.S. financing costs.

Thus the contest between Bessent and the Japanese government is no longer just about exchange rates; it also involves BOJ rate‑hike speed, government spending, tax cuts, defence budgeting, Japanese bond yields and the interaction of the world’s two largest sovereign‑debt markets. For Kishida’s government, balancing economic stimulus, cost‑of‑living pressures and market demands for fiscal discipline will be the core policy challenge going forward.

items.title: 植田談話恐令市場失望？日銀利率決議出爐前夕　富國銀行高調做空日元、花旗估將跌向159
items.title_en: Will Ueda's Remarks Disappoint the Market? On the Eve of the BOJ Rate Decision, Wells Fargo Shorts the Yen Aggressively, Citi Forecasts a Drop to 159
paras: 日本央行(BOJ)公布最新利率決議前夕，外匯策略師普遍預期「升息容易、表態難鷹」，日元短線偏向貶值。掉期市場數據幾乎完全計入升息1碼，焦點轉向BOJ總裁植田和男記者會對後續節奏的指引。日元在今日亞洲匯市早盤小貶約0.1%至156.15。
富國銀行策略師Chidu Narayanan表示，BOJ要達到甚至超越市場鷹派預期「門檻​​很高」，會議結果若僅兌現升息、不明示連續緊縮，風險傾向偏鴿，建議做空日元。
ING Bank NV的G10外匯策略主管Chris Turner預估，若BOJ未能釋放進一步升息訊號，日元兌美元將貶至157或158水平，花旗策略師Daniel Tobon更預估未來幾週日元可能貶向159。
壓低日元反彈的是美日利差。聯準會(Fed)週三宣布升息1碼至3.75%—4%，主席華許暗示通膨偏高、必要時繼續收緊，美元指數站上100，美債短端利率走高，
不過，策略師們對中長線判斷分化；花旗認為日本近期匯率與貨幣政策調整屬「制度轉變」一部分，長期仍利於日元；荷蘭銀行資深外匯策略師Georgette Boele則預期能源價格暫時抑制反彈，2027年第一季前美元兌日元將在154附近交易，2027下半年隨Fed、歐洲央行(ECB)降息才轉強。整體來看，短線市場以「鴿派升息」防日元回貶，158—160為關鍵觀察區。
paras_en: Ahead of the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) latest rate decision, most FX strategists expect a "rate hike is easy, hawkish guidance is hard," implying short‑term yen weakness. Swap market data almost fully priced in a 10‑basis‑point hike, shifting focus to the guidance on future pacing from BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda's press conference. The yen slipped about 0.1% to 156.15 in early Asian trading today.

Wells Fargo strategist Chidu Narayanan said the BOJ faces a very high hurdle to meet or exceed market hawkish expectations. If the meeting only delivers a hike without signalling further tightening, the bias leans dovish, so he recommends shorting the yen.

ING Bank NV’s G10 FX strategy head Chris Turner projected that if the BOJ fails to signal additional hikes, the yen will fall to the 157‑158 level against the dollar, while Citi strategist Daniel Tobon sees the yen possibly sliding toward 159 in the coming weeks.

The yen’s downside is being capped by the US‑Japan rate differential. The Fed raised rates by one quarter point on Wednesday to a 3.75%‑4% range, with Chair Powell hinting that inflation remains elevated and further tightening may be needed. The dollar index is above 100 and short‑term US Treasury yields are rising.

However, strategists diverge on the medium‑to‑long term. Citi views Japan’s recent exchange‑rate and policy moves as part of a "structural shift" that will ultimately benefit the yen, while senior ING FX strategist Georgette Boele expects energy prices to temporarily suppress a rebound, forecasting the dollar‑yen around 154 before Q1 2027 and only strengthening in the second half of 2027 after rate cuts by the Fed and ECB. Overall, the short‑term market is watching the "dovish hike" narrative to prevent a yen rebound, with 158‑160 as the key observation zone.
